Both of these compounds are implicated in the activation of ATR, a serine/threonine-protein kinase. The scores from the two paths indicate a moderate level of confidence in the proposed pathway, with slight variations in the strength of the evidence. The shared involvement of G(I)/G(S)/G(O) subunit gamma-2 as a mediator in the activation of ATR suggests a possible mechanism where androstenedione may influence the activity of this protein through its interaction with these secondary targets. The evidence supports a plausible pathway, but further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the direct relationship between androstenedione and ATR.
